html:
The Ulwa are a small Indigenous people of the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua, whose main village, Karawala, lies near the mouth of the Río Grande de Matagalpa. Their language is close to that of the Mayangna, and both belong to the Misumalpan family along with Miskito.

The Ulwa lived by farming, fishing and hunting along the rivers. From the 1600s the Miskito, armed by British traders, came to dominate the Mosquito Coast, and many Ulwa and other Sumu peoples paid them tribute or took up Miskito ways. Today only a few hundred people still speak Ulwa.
